title: Parkinson's mechanisms 1: what losing dopamine neurons does to the fly brain's wiring
written: 2026-11-03T20:26Z, before any of this analysis was run.
question: When dopamine neurons are lost, as in fruit-fly models of Parkinson's disease, which neurons and brain regions lose their dopamine input, how quickly, and where are the single points of failure?
brain: FlyWire v783 (female brain). Dopamine neurons and their connections from the FlyWire release (connections of 5+ synapses, with brain region per connection).
dopamine_neurons: FlyWire class 'DAN': 331 neurons (PAM 307, PPL1 16, PPL2 8). Dopamine neurons outside this class (e.g. PPM and PAL clusters) are not labelled DAN in FlyWire and are not included; this is a stated limitation.
scenarios: PPL1 first: the 16 PPL1 neurons lost one at a time (a cluster often reported vulnerable in fly Parkinson's models), then the rest at random.
PAM only: PAM neurons lost at random, 0 to 100%.
All dopamine neurons at random, 0 to 100% in 10% steps. Random orders use fixed seeds (10 orders); results report the average and range.
measures: For every neuron that receives dopamine-neuron connections: the share of its dopamine input synapses that remain.
Grouped by FlyWire cell class and by brain region (neuropil).
Neurons that lose half or more of their dopamine input, at each stage.
Single points of failure: neurons whose dopamine input comes from 2 or fewer dopamine neurons.
Fast-signal check with the published brain model (Shiu et al. 2024 settings): all 331 dopamine neurons removed, sugar 100/s and water 200/s, 30 repeats; change in MN9 firing.
not_claimed: Dopamine in real brains mostly changes how strongly other neurons are connected (for example, it drives learning in the mushroom body) and acts slowly; the simulation treats it as a fast signal. This analysis maps WHERE the dopamine signal would be lost and how robust each target is; it does not simulate the disease chemistry (such as alpha-synuclein), cell death itself, or behaviour. Exploratory: there is no real-fly measurement of this kind to check it against.
